items.text: All provisions of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984

segments.text: The Qanun-e-Shahadat Order governs what facts may be proved, how evidence is produced and how courts assess different forms of proof in judicial proceedings.

The easiest map is: relevancy of facts → admissions/confessions → statements by unavailable persons → expert and character evidence → documentary/oral evidence → burden of proof → witnesses and examination. Evidence law is about the connection between a fact in issue and the material offered to prove or disprove it.
Primary authority: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984, current official text.

Evidence law controls the material that may lawfully be used to prove or disprove facts in judicial proceedings. Its basic discipline is to move from the fact in issue to legally relevant material and then to the method by which that material is proved. This prevents a court from deciding a case on every piece of information that happens to exist.

Three questions should be kept separate: Is the fact relevant? Is the proposed material admissible under the governing rules? Has the fact actually been proved to the required legal standard? A relevant item can still fail because it is not proved in the legally required manner.

Start with facts in issue and relevant facts. Then study admissions and confessions, statements made in legally recognized circumstances, opinion and expert evidence, character evidence where relevant, oral and documentary proof, presumptions, burden of proof, competence of witnesses and the sequence of examination.

Documentary proof requires special attention because authenticity, primary and secondary evidence, electronic records and presumptions may determine whether a document can be relied upon. The existence of a photocopy, screenshot or electronic file does not automatically establish its legal authenticity.

The burden of proof allocates responsibility for establishing a proposition. A presumption may require a court to draw, permit it to draw, or regulate the evidentiary treatment of a fact according to the governing provision. The burden can also shift in a practical sense as evidence is produced, but this should not be confused with the ultimate legal burden where the law fixes it.

Examination-in-chief allows a party to present its witness; cross-examination tests accuracy, credibility, perception, memory and consistency within the rules of evidence; re-examination ordinarily clarifies matters arising from cross-examination. Effective evidence analysis therefore combines admissibility with reliability.

items.text: Evidence law answers a basic question:
what material may a court legally use to decide whether a disputed fact is proved? The first step is always to identify the fact in issue and then ask whether the offered fact is legally relevant.
Relevancy and proof are related but different. A fact may be relevant yet still require proper proof through an admissible witness, document, presumption or other legally recognized method.

Admissions and confessions concern statements that can have evidentiary consequences; documentary and oral evidence have different rules; expert evidence assists the court on specialized matters but does not automatically decide the case.

The burden of proof tells us who must establish a proposition. Presumptions may alter how that burden operates. The standard and allocation of proof must always be connected to the type of proceeding and issue.

Witness examination is a process for presenting and testing testimony: examination-in-chief presents the witness's evidence, cross-examination tests it, and re-examination may clarify matters arising from cross-examination.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not say that every piece of information collected by a party is “evidence.” Evidence must satisfy legal rules of relevancy, admissibility and proof.

items.text: Make separate charts for oral evidence, documentary evidence and presumptions.
Prepare burden of proof and examination of witnesses carefully.
Use the official current Qanun-e-Shahadat text for exact articles.

segments.text: Evidence answers score when rules are linked to purpose: reliability, fairness and proof of disputed facts.
Accuracy note: Pakistan Code publishes the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 as the governing federal evidence instrument; use the latest official text for amendments.
Not every fact is legally relevant.
Relevancy decides whether a fact can connect to the dispute.
Burden of proof determines who must establish a fact.
Witness examination normally moves through examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination.
Documentary evidence has specific proof rules.
